narrative: 摇臂上升从人体高度出发，然后离开这个高度。人物先是留在画面中，接着是屋顶，再接着是整座城市。
到最后，那个人物只剩下夜色中的一件深色外套。当一场戏需要结束，或者一个私密时刻必须承认包裹着它的整个世界时，就用这个镜头。
向上摇（Tilt Up）只改变角度，而摇臂改变的是整幅地图。
不要把它当作每个全景镜头的装饰。如果摄影机上升时没有出现任何新信息，这个运动就是空洞的。
how: 操作员坐在摇臂上或通过遥控云台操作摇臂。摇臂可以只有几英尺长（小摇臂/Jib），也可以长达数十英尺（长臂摇臂/Technocrane）。
上升过程中保留一个可见的前景锚点，让新揭示出的尺度有参照物。提示词中要写明“摇臂上升并稍稍后退”，标明起幅位置（肩高、腰部、特写），并说明所揭示的内容（屋顶、峡谷、天桥）。
如果只写“摄影机上升”，得到的往往只是一个上摇镜头或廉价的变焦效果。
when: 用它来结束一场戏、揭示一座城市，或把人物转变为风景的一部分。具体场景：一名女子站在湿漉漉的屋顶上，随后楼下的广场占满画面。
如果结尾画面没有揭示出开头画面未曾暗示的任何信息，就不要使用摇臂上升。
vs: 向上摇（Tilt Up）是在固定三脚架上的旋转。小摇臂镜头（Jib Shot）则是这一类运动中短臂的版本。
航拍拉远（Aerial Pullback）会持续到直升机或高空无人机高度、地理景观完全占据主导。拉镜头（Pull Out）则始终停留在平视高度，只做后退。
摇臂下降（Crane Down）是抵达一张面孔，而不是离开它。
examples_film: 《历劫佳人》（Touch of Evil）的开场把摇臂运动当作一句贯穿边境小镇的长句。《乱世佳人》（Gone with the Wind）中伤员遍野的后拉镜头，把一个人变成了战争统计数字中的一员。
《爱乐之城》（La La Land）用山坡和码头上的摇臂镜头，把爱情安放进一座真实的城市。《大玩家》（The Player）以片场调度的摇臂长镜头开场。
这是语法，不是可以直接照搬的画面。
mistakes: 常见的错误近亲是向上摇（Tilt Up），或是从特写直接剪切到航拍。破绽在于没有视差，或者尺度发生跳跃却没有连续的上升过程。
修正方法：真实的物理上升加上少许向外伸展，保留一个可见的前景锚点，让人物在整个上升过程中保持连续可见。

faq.q: 电影中的“摇臂上升”是什么？
faq.a: 这是用小摇臂或摇臂将摄影机实际抬升的运动，往往同时略微后退，使人物尺度的画面变成对这个地方更宽广的呈现。

faq.q: 摇臂上升 与 向上摇 的区别
faq.a: 上摇是摄影机在固定三脚架上的旋转，而摇臂运动是摄影机在空间中的实际位移，因此前景、中景和背景会产生视差变化。

faq.q: 什么时候该使用摇臂上升？
faq.a: 当一场戏应该收尾，或者一个私密时刻必须承认容纳它的城市、人群或土地时使用。如果上升过程没有揭示任何新内容，就不要使用。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写摇臂上升的提示词？
faq.a: 写明起始高度、“摇臂上升并稍稍后退”，以及所揭示的内容。示例：camera cranes up and slightly back from shoulder height, revealing rooftops and the city beyond.

narrative: A crane-up starts at human height and leaves it. The person stays in frame, then the rooftops, then the city.
By the end, the figure is one dark coat in a much larger night. Use it when the scene needs to end, or when a private moment has to admit the world that contains it.
A tilt up only changes the angle. A crane changes the map.
Do not use it as decoration on every wide. If nothing new appears as the camera climbs, the move is empty.
how: The operator rides or remote-heads a crane. The arm can be a few feet (a jib) or tens of feet (a Technocrane).

Keep a foreground anchor visible during the rise so the newly revealed scale has a reference. Prompt crane up and slightly back, name the start (shoulder height, waist, close-up), and name the reveal (rooftops, canyon, overpass).
If you only write camera goes up, you often get a tilt or a cheap zoom.
when: Use it to end a scene, reveal a city, or turn a person into landscape. Concrete beat: a woman on a wet roof, then the square below takes the frame.
Do not crane up if the last frame shows nothing the first frame did not already imply.
vs: A Tilt Up rotates on a fixed tripod. A Jib Shot is the short-arm version of this family.
An Aerial Pullback continues until geography wins completely from helicopter or high-drone height. A Pull Out stays at eye height and only retreats.
Crane Down arrives at a face instead of leaving one.
examples_film: The opening of Touch of Evil treats the crane as a long sentence through a border town. The wounded-field pullaway in Gone with the Wind turns a person into a statistic of war.
La La Land lets hillside and dock cranes sit romance in a real city. The Player opens on studio-lot crane choreography.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Tilt Up or a cut from close-up to aerial. The tell is no parallax, or a jump in scale with no continuous ascent.
The fix: physical rise plus a little boom-out, a visible foreground anchor, continuity of the figure all the way up.

faq.q: What is Crane Up in film?
faq.a: It is a physical lift of the camera on a jib or crane, often easing back, so a human-scale frame becomes a wider view of the place.
A tilt rotates the camera on a fixed tripod. A crane physically moves the camera through space, so foreground, mid-ground, and background change in parallax.

faq.q: When should I use Crane Up?
faq.a: When a scene should close, or a private beat must admit the city, crowd, or land that contains it. Do not use it if the climb reveals nothing new.

faq.q: How do I prompt Crane Up for AI image or video?
faq.a: Name starting height, crane up and slightly back, and what is revealed. Example: camera cranes up and slightly back from shoulder height, revealing rooftops and the city beyond.
